findings.title: Locksmith's picks: the early line
findings.text: The strategy Locksmith publishes (bet when it disagrees with the opening moneyline or total) went 3025-2516 for +278 units (+5.0%) from 2021-22 to today, profitable in 6 of 6 seasons. Each season used only rules that had already worked before it. Early moneyline bets beat the closing line 72% of the time.

findings.title: The edge is the early line
findings.text: When Locksmith disagreed with the OPENING moneyline by 6% or more, the line then moved toward Locksmith: those bets beat the closing line 64% of the time and returned +6.1% on 945 bets (2019-20, 2021-22, 2022-23). Bet early; the value is gone once the line moves.

findings.title: Totals move toward Locksmith too
findings.text: When Locksmith's total was 0.4+ goals away from the opening total, the line moved Locksmith's way 30% of the time and against it only 1%. Bets at the opener won 55.3% (1031 bets; 52.4% breaks even at −110).

findings.title: Betting at the closing line doesn't pay
findings.text: Rules picked season by season and bet at the final price went 717-688 (-1.8% return, -26 units). The closing line already knows what Locksmith knows, so every hockey pick is an early-line pick.

findings.title: Close to the sharpest line, not better
findings.text: On 8,209 games with real closing lines, Locksmith's win chances scored 0.6646 (log loss) against the closing line's 0.6606. That is close (a coin flip scores 0.693), but the market is still slightly sharper at game time.

findings.title: What actually moves a hockey game
findings.text: In the goal model fitted on 21,000 team-games: home ice adds 7% goals, the 2nd night of a back-to-back costs 5%, a goalie who saves 0.5 goals a game above average takes 17% off the other team's scoring, and 5-on-5 shot quality matters far more than power plays.

findings.title: At the game-day price, the edge is gone
findings.text: Early moneylines with a 3%+ edge at the opener returned +3.2% per bet at the opening price but -0.6% at the closing price (4,431 bets). The value is in betting before the market moves; a pick is shown only while today's price still beats what bets like it have won.

findings.title: Honest chances: what bets like this actually won
findings.text: Every pick shows the chance that early bets like it actually won, not the simulator's own number. Early moneylines returned +2.0% per bet at 3%-5% edge, -5.8% per bet at 5%-7% edge, +4.3% per bet at 7%-10% edge, +18.0% per bet at 10%+ edge; early totals won 53% at 0.3-0.45 goals off the opener, 55% at 0.45-0.6 goals off the opener, 58% at 0.6-0.8 goals off the opener, 62% at 0.8+ goals off the opener.

findings.title: Player props: the line moves Locksmith's way, the price is still tight
findings.text: Graded on 4,899 real DraftKings over/unders this season at the OPENING line and price (closing prices on finished games can be in-game prices, so they are only used when set before puck drop). DraftKings' opener is still slightly more accurate than Locksmith alone, but when Locksmith disagreed, the price moved toward Locksmith before the game 60% of the time (69% on big disagreements; shots on goal 69%). Prop rules picked day by day from earlier days only went 181-129 (+2.2%). Anytime-goal and milestone prices lost money at every edge level, so Locksmith never bets them. Overs hit less often than priced (38% vs 40%).

findings.title: Player projections: ice time by situation beats averages
findings.text: Projecting each skater from his even-strength and power-play ice time, his rates in each situation and tonight's opponent and goalie beat both the old method and season averages on all 49,616 player-games of 2025-26 (anytime-goal log loss 0.3939 vs 0.3967 old and 0.4825 season average; 1+ point 0.5946 vs 0.6017 and 0.6894).

findings.title: Who is in the lineup matters
findings.text: Every 5-on-5 shift since 2018 (3.1 million of them) was used to measure each skater's impact on expected goals, adjusted for teammates and opponents. Tonight's lineup strength is now part of the goal model and is clearly significant: a team missing its best players is rated accordingly. Top impact right now: Quinn Hughes, Evan Bouchard, Sean Walker, Travis Sanheim, Thomas Harley.

findings.title: Shot quality beats shot counts
findings.text: Locksmith's expected-goals model scores 500,455 recent shots with an AUC of 0.75, using distance, angle, shot type, rebounds and rushes. Teams' expected goals predict future scoring better than their actual goals, which is why the ratings lean on them.
